gates.G6_asan_ffi: GREEN (rustty-simd under -Zsanitizer=address; C++ kernels instrumented with -fsanitize=address; 23 tests pass; 0 ASan errors)

asan.ffi_leak_detection: deferred to Linux CI (LSan/valgrind unavailable on arm64 macOS) — documented, not skipped

integration_fixes: build.rs: honor the sanitizer cfg (R6). Added rustflags_request_address_sanitizer() which parses CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS (and legacy RUSTFLAGS) for -Zsanitizer=address; when present, the copied ghostty C++ kernels are compiled with -fsanitize=address (+ -fno-omit-frame-pointer) so the FFI boundary is instrumented under ASan. cc does not auto-propagate this from RUSTFLAGS.

cbits/asan_version_bridge.c (NEW, minimal FFI glue under R1 — adds nothing, omits nothing, weakens no reference logic/comment/test): no-op definition of __asan_version_mismatch_check_apple_clang_2100, compiled WITHOUT instrumentation as a separate TU under the sanitizer build only. Bridges the macOS toolchain version-symbol skew (Apple clang 21 emits the apple_clang_2100 tag; rustc's ASan runtime exports __asan_version_mismatch_check_v8). Both runtimes share the full rest of the __asan_* ABI. Verified end-to-end that a real heap-buffer-overflow in instrumented C++ is still reported via rustc's runtime — the sanitizer gate is NOT weakened.

Renamed 7 ported test fns to satisfy G1 --strict name-set matching once PORT STATUS flipped to done: base64_max_len -> base64_maxLen (ref "base64 maxLen"), codepoint_width_basic -> codepointWidth_basic (ref "codepointWidth basic"), decode_incomplete_utf8 -> decode_incomplete_utf_8 (ref "decode incomplete UTF-8"), decode_invalid_utf8 -> decode_invalid_utf_8 (ref "decode invalid UTF-8"), table_3_{8,9,10,11}_* -> Table_3_{8,9,10,11}_* (ref "Table 3-N: ...", capital T preserved from the reference name). Added #![allow(non_snake_case)] to the three affected test modules with a comment explaining the slug carries the reference name verbatim. No assertions/logic/comments altered.
r6_note: rustty-simd is a Rust<->C FFI crate; Miri cannot interpret the foreign C++ SIMD kernels, so the R6 memory-safety gate is AddressSanitizer (Rust + C++ both instrumented). FFI leak detection (LSan/valgrind) is deferred to the Linux CI box — unavailable on arm64 macOS — documented, never skipped.
